cleanIntro: The Maxus II is Browning's gas gun: high-pressure gas from two barrel ports drives a piston sleeve and gas piston riding on the magazine tube, and that assembly — not inertia, not recoil — cycles the bolt. Gas guns pay for their soft shooting in carbon, and this manual is honest about where: the magazine tube, the piston and the inside of the piston sleeve are the dirty parts, and the book's own tool of choice for them is a green Scotch-Brite kitchen pad. The published teardown is deep — barrel and gas system off for routine cleaning, then the Lightning Trigger group on two pins and the bolt assembly out for a complete cleaning, both designed as field jobs without special tools. Two hard boundaries hold everywhere: the action is never slammed closed with the barrel off, and neither the trigger group, the bolt assembly nor the piston's internal spring goes apart further than the book shows.

steps.title: Gauge, chamber and cycling loads off the barrel inscription
steps.action: The gauge and chamber length are inscribed on the side of the barrel, and the length rule is absolute — no 3-inch or 3½-inch shells in a 2¾-inch chamber, no 3½-inch in a 3-inch. Being a gas autoloader, the Maxus II also has a published floor for what cycles it: 3-inch guns run all 12-gauge 2¾ and 3-inch 1 oz-and-heavier factory lead and steel loads; 3½-inch guns the same 1 oz floor across all three lengths. Below that floor the gas system may not receive enough impulse, and a short-cycling gas gun is almost always an ammunition or fouling problem, in that order.
steps.prose: Examine every shell against the inscription, not against the rest of the box.
steps.quote: Maxus II 12 gauge, 3" chamber models will shoot all 12 gauge, 2¾" and 3", 1 oz. and heavier factory lead and steel target loads. Maxus II 12 gauge, 3½" chamber models will shoot all 1 oz. and heavier factory lead and steel 12 gauge, 2¾", 3" and 3½" field loads.
steps.cite: MAXUS II SHOTGUN Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Ammunition
steps.warn: Chamber length is a pressure rule; load weight is a cycling rule. Both come off the barrel.

steps.title: Safety at the rear of the trigger guard — verify which hand yours is set for
steps.action: Press the safety button at the rear of the trigger guard to the right for on safe; left exposes the red warning band. The factory installs it right-handed, but a gunsmith can reverse it — a reversed safety shows its red band on the right side of the guard instead — so verify the installation on your own gun before trusting any direction words, including this guide's. And Browning's standing caveat: the red band is paint and can wear away; do not depend on the colour alone.
steps.prose: This manual's instructions are written for the right-handed installation, and so are these steps.
steps.quote: To place the firearm on safe, press the “safety” button to the right.
steps.cite: MAXUS II SHOTGUN Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Operation of the "Safety"
steps.warn: A reversed safety mirrors every direction in this guide. Check yours first.

steps.title: Speed Unload at the shell stop, then prove the chamber
steps.action: Safety on, muzzle safe. Turn the gun trigger-guard-up and find the shell stop inside the receiver on the right side of the loading port — visually to the left as you look down into it. Push it inward with your index finger and the magazine spring hands you a shell; catch it, press again, and repeat until the tube gives nothing more. Then pull the bolt handle rearward to eject any chambered shell, lock the bolt open, feel the magazine opening with a finger for a shell that never fed, and inspect chamber, feed mechanism and magazine by eye.
steps.prose: The carrier's edges are sharp — the manual warns about fingers and gloves at the loading port, and unloading uses the same real estate.
steps.quote: 3. Push inward on the shell stop with your index finger (Figure 14) to release a shell from the magazine. As the shell stop is pressed in, a shell will be forced out of the magazine under spring pressure. Catch the shell in your hand as it comes out.
steps.cite: MAXUS II SHOTGUN Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Unloading > Speed Unloading
steps.warn: Shells come out under spring pressure. An empty tube still proves nothing about the chamber.

steps.title: The barrel-off law: the bolt never slams home on an empty receiver
steps.action: Fix the rule before the magazine cap moves, because every procedure from here runs inside it: with the barrel out of the receiver, the bolt release button is never pressed free. Released, the bolt runs forward with nothing to stop it and the bolt handle strikes the receiver. When a step needs the bolt forward with the barrel off — and the trigger-group and bolt-assembly steps do — the move is made by holding the bolt handle, pressing the release, and letting the bolt walk forward under your hand.
steps.prose: The manual prints this warning at assembly, disassembly, both adaptor procedures, the trigger-group section and the bolt section. That repetition is data about how often it happens.
steps.quote: NEVER ALLOW THE ACTION TO SLAM CLOSED BY PRESSING THE BOLT RELEASE BUTTON WITHOUT THE BARREL INSTALLED.
steps.cite: MAXUS II SHOTGUN Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Assembly, step 1 (repeated at Disassembly and in both three-shot adaptor procedures)
steps.warn: Barrel off = bolt moves forward only under a controlled hand.

steps.title: Forearm off, then barrel and gas system forward off the magazine tube
steps.action: Lock the bolt rearward by pulling the bolt handle fully to the rear. Unscrew the magazine cap and slide the forearm forward off the magazine tube — without squeezing the open rear end if it is wood. Then, for cleaning, slide the barrel and the gas system components forward and off the magazine tube together. The gas bracket, piston sleeve and gas piston are what you are holding: the parts the powder gas actually works through, and the reason a Maxus II strip goes one layer deeper than its inertia stablemates before the receiver is even open.
steps.prose: For storage instead of cleaning, the barrel comes off alone and the forearm goes back on the tube — two compact units.
steps.quote: 3. For cleaning, remove the barrel and gas system components by sliding them forward and off the magazine tube. See “Cleaning and Maintenance Suggestions” for cleaning procedures.
steps.cite: MAXUS II SHOTGUN Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Disassembly, steps 1-3

steps.title: Field strip complete — gas system in hand, receiver work in the deep branch
steps.action: Barrel, forearm, gas piston, piston sleeve and sleeve spring on the mat is the Maxus II's routine cleaning state, and the manual grades what remains: normal maintenance with the barrel on, careful cleaning with barrel and gas system off, and a complete cleaning — trigger group and bolt assembly out of the receiver — when the action is excessively dirty or wet. That complete teardown is the Deep Clean branch, inside the manual's boundary line: disassembly of the action means the bolt assembly and trigger group, and beyond that only a qualified gunsmith.
steps.prose: The bolt stays locked rearward the whole time the gun sits in this state — the slam-closed rule is now live and stays live until the barrel returns.
steps.quote: Disassembly of the action involves the removal of the bolt assembly and the trigger group. Disassembly beyond this point should only be performed by a qualified gunsmith.
steps.cite: MAXUS II SHOTGUN Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Removal of the Trigger Group

steps.title: The gas system: solvent, nylon, Scotch-Brite — and two absolute nevers
steps.action: Spray the magazine tube, gas piston and piston sleeve with gun solvent and brush them thoroughly with a NYLON brush; take the piston sleeve spring off the sleeve to reach the sleeve's interior, and spray inside the gas piston. For the baked-on carbon that gas guns grow on the magazine tube and inside the piston, the manual's own recommendation is a green Scotch-Brite kitchen pad. The two boundaries are printed in capitals right in the procedure: do not attempt to remove the spring inside the piston, and never use a steel brush on any gas system component. Finish with a very light film of oil on all gas parts.
steps.prose: Carbon here is the Maxus II's whole failure budget — a gun that short-cycles on good ammunition almost always fixes itself in this step.
steps.quote: DO NOT ATTEMPT TO REMOVE THE SPRING INSIDE OF THE PISTON. NEVER USE A STEEL BRUSH ON ANY OF THE GAS SYSTEM COMPONENTS.
steps.cite: MAXUS II SHOTGUN Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — CLEANING THE GAS SYSTEM, step 2
steps.warn: Nylon and Scotch-Brite only. The piston's internal spring stays in the piston.

steps.title: Bore from the breech, choke tube out with its own wrench
steps.action: With the barrel off: rod, slotted tip or jag, snug lightly-oiled patch in at the breech end and back and forth. Inspect both ends for leading and plastic wad streaks — normal amounts near the muzzle and ahead of the chamber are expected; excess comes off with a bronze brush soaked in powder solvent, pushed fully through before withdrawing. Pull the choke tube, wipe tube, tube threads and barrel threads with a nylon brush and oil lightly, and respect the system rule: Invector-DS tubes are for back-bored Browning barrels only and never interchange with Invector-Plus or Standard Invector.
steps.prose: Dry patch, then a final oiled patch, then the check for patches left behind — a forgotten patch is a bore obstruction at the next shot.
steps.caution: Only the supplied T-wrench, only the correct system, and never fired without a tube installed.
steps.quote: BROWNING INVECTOR-DS CHOKE TUBES ARE FOR USE ONLY IN BROWNING SHOTGUNS WITH BACK-BORED BARRELS, AND ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE WITH BROWNING STANDARD INVECTOR OR INVECTOR-PLUS CHOKE TUBES.
steps.cite: MAXUS II SHOTGUN Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Interchangeable Choke Tube System (bore: CLEANING THE BARREL, steps 3-6)

steps.title: Rails, films and the choke-section quirk worth knowing about
steps.action: The receiver's specific lube point is a drop of lightweight gun oil on each rail the bolt runs on — set at initial cleaning and refreshed occasionally. After weather or grit, wipe the principal working parts clean and re-film them lightly; excess oil in the action runs back into the stock wood and loosens the stock, so films, never pours. One documentation quirk to read past: the choke section of this book opens with a warning that names the BT-99 — a different Browning — while stating the practice that applies to every choke job on any gun: action open, gun verified completely unloaded first.
steps.prose: That stray model name is the manual's error to note, not a reason to skip the practice it states.
steps.caution: The warning names the BT-99 — a printing quirk in this book. The unloaded-first practice binds regardless.
steps.quote: WHENEVER REMOVING OR INSTALLING A CHOKE TUBE IN YOUR BT-99 SHOTGUN, ALWAYS OPEN THE ACTION AND MAKE ABSOLUTELY CERTAIN THE SHOTGUN IS COMPLETELY UNLOADED.
steps.cite: MAXUS II SHOTGUN Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Interchangeable Choke Tube System, opening warning (oiling: PERIODIC OILING)

steps.title: Extra barrels swap within gauge and chamber — same three nevers as every Browning
steps.action: Maxus II barrels interchange within a given gauge and chamber length with no fitting. The restrictions are the familiar absolutes: never a 3½-inch-chambered barrel on a 3-inch gun or the reverse, never another manufacturer's barrel however similar it looks, and never a barrel from any other Browning shotgun model. The TurnKey three-shot adaptor lives under the same discipline — bolt locked back, forearm off, a key or flat screwdriver pressed in and quarter-turned in the magazine tube slot — and its procedures end by reinstalling the gas piston, barrel, forearm and cap in that order.
steps.prose: Both adaptor procedures carry the slam-closed warning inline, because the forearm is off and the barrel loose exactly when people get careless.
steps.quote: Never use a barrel from any other Browning shotgun.
steps.cite: MAXUS II SHOTGUN Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Extra Barrels (adaptor: Three-Shot Adapter (Plug))
steps.warn: Wrong chamber, other maker, other Browning model: all barred.

deepSteps.title: Lightning Trigger group out on two pins
deepSteps.action: With the gun verified empty and the barrel off, walk the bolt forward under control — bolt handle held, release pressed, eased home. Push the two trigger guard pins through the receiver with a punch, working from either side and pulling them out the opposite side, careful of the receiver's finish. Grasp the trigger guard and pull it up and out. Clean the group with a quality aerosol gun solvent, let it dry, then oil the moving parts very lightly. The boundary is printed where you stop: do not disassemble the trigger group beyond this point.
deepSteps.prose: Browning designed this as a field job with no special tools — 'excessively dirty or wet' is the trigger for doing it, not round count.
deepSteps.quote: DO NOT DISASSEMBLE THE TRIGGER GROUP BEYOND THIS POINT.
deepSteps.cite: MAXUS II SHOTGUN Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Removing the Trigger Group
deepSteps.warn: Two pins, out and back whole. Nothing inside the group is user-serviceable.

deepSteps.title: Bolt assembly out: handle first, then forward off the rails
deepSteps.action: With barrel, gas piston, piston sleeve and sleeve spring already off — and preferably the trigger group out first, as the manual prefers — walk the bolt forward under control. Pull the bolt handle straight outward and it comes free. Press the bolt release and slide the bolt assembly forward and out of the receiver. The bolt and bolt slide can now be separated for cleaning, and that separation is the published limit: do not disassemble the bolt assembly beyond this point.
deepSteps.prose: The straight-out bolt handle is the step that surprises first-timers — no pin, no tool, just a firm pull.
deepSteps.quote: DO NOT DISASSEMBLE THE BOLT ASSEMBLY BEYOND THIS POINT.
deepSteps.cite: MAXUS II SHOTGUN Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Servicing the Bolt Assembly > REMOVING THE BOLT ASSEMBLY
deepSteps.warn: Bolt and bolt slide separate — firing pin and internals stay put.

deepSteps.title: Receiver cavity cleaned, then everything home in the right order
deepSteps.action: With trigger group and bolt out, clean the receiver cavity with gun solvent and a nylon brush for caked grime, wipe it clean, oil it lightly and wipe dry — the manual states no further disassembly is required for cleaning, and means it. Rebuild in reverse: bolt and bolt slide reassembled, a few drops of oil in the bolt's grooves for the slide rails, rails aligned with the receiver grooves and the assembly inserted bolt-slide-link end first with the release pressed. The critical engagement is the bolt slide link seating in the socket of the recoil spring follower — guide it in, replace the bolt handle in its slot, and open and close the action several times to prove the link and follower are engaged.
deepSteps.prose: Then the trigger group: bolt forward, group in, holes aligned, pins tapped home with a plastic or wooden mallet. The slam-closed rule holds until the barrel is back on.
deepSteps.quote: 4. Ensure the bolt slide link fits into the socket in the recoil spring follower (Figure 33).
deepSteps.cite: MAXUS II SHOTGUN Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — REINSTALLATION OF THE BOLT ASSEMBLY (cavity: Cleaning the Action)
deepSteps.warn: A bolt slide link that missed its socket feels fine until the first shot. Cycle several times and feel the spring engage.

cleaning.name: GAS SYSTEM (the Maxus II's real work)
tasks: Magazine tube, gas piston and piston sleeve sprayed with gun solvent, nylon-brushed thoroughly
Piston sleeve spring off the sleeve to reach the sleeve interior; spray inside the gas piston
Green Scotch-Brite pad for heavy carbon on the tube and inside the piston — the manual's own tool
NEVER a steel brush on any gas component; NEVER remove the spring inside the piston
Very light oil film on all gas parts to finish

cleaning.name: BARREL & CHOKE (barrel off, from the breech)
tasks: Rod and snug lightly-oiled patch in at the breech; read the lead/plastic streaks before scrubbing
Bronze brush with powder solvent for excess, pushed fully through before withdrawing
Choke tube out with the supplied T-wrench; tube, tube threads and barrel threads nylon-brushed and lightly oiled
Dry patch, final oiled patch, then check for forgotten patches

cleaning.name: RECEIVER, BOLT RAILS & ACTION
tasks: A drop of lightweight oil on each receiver rail the bolt rides on
Complete cleaning (deep): receiver cavity solvent-cleaned, nylon-brushed, wiped, lightly oiled and wiped dry
Trigger group: aerosol solvent, air dry, very light oil — never opened further
No pours: excess oil in the action ends up in the stock wood

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR & WOOD
tasks: Exposed metal wiped with an oiled cloth until finger marks are gone
Keep insect repellents, sunscreen and strong chemicals off the finishes
Wood: light gun oil or quality furniture wax — never both

reassembly: Bolt locked rearward before assembly starts, and it stays there until step by step says otherwise.

Gas system home first if it was off: piston sleeve and gas piston slid push-rod-end first onto the magazine tube, push rod aligned with the slot in the LEFT side of the receiver, gas system spring properly positioned.
Barrel extension aligned with the top of the receiver, gas bracket over the magazine tube, extension seated solidly — then confirm the push rod moves freely in its receiver slot.
Forearm over the magazine tube and gas bracket until it seats securely; magazine cap fully tightened clockwise.
Open and close the action several times, then retighten the magazine cap — the manual's own final assembly step.
Only with the barrel installed may the bolt release drop the bolt free.
Confirm the safety shows no red band on safe, in the orientation your gun's safety is installed.
fncheck: With the gun assembled and verified empty: cycle the bolt and feel it run home crisply — sluggish return after cleaning usually means too much oil, not too little. Confirm the bolt locks open on an empty magazine and drops cleanly on the release with the barrel installed. Confirm the magazine cap stayed tight after the cycling test, the choke tube is seated, and the safety blocks the trigger on safe. If the bolt assembly was out, the proof that the bolt slide link found its recoil-spring-follower socket is several smooth full cycles against spring resistance. Never test the mechanical function with live ammunition.
